character.centerRule: Jesus Christ remains the same Scripture person across Jesus, the Christ, Messiah, Jesus Christ, and Christ Jesus forms. Christ is essential to the identity record but is observed as title-to-combined-name development rather than treated as a hereditary surname.

phases.orientation: Read earlier sources beside the later Scripture texts that quote, apply, or reuse them; keep promise, later claim, and traditional interpretation distinct.
phases.title: Promise and Anticipation

phases.orientation: Read the distinct genealogies, announcements, birth witnesses, journeys, Temple scenes, childhood, and opening Word-language without flattening their witnesses.
phases.title: Genealogy, Birth, and Childhood

phases.orientation: Follow baptism, wilderness testing, first testimony, first followers, and the opening proclamation in each Gospel setting.
phases.title: Baptism, Testing, and Beginning

phases.orientation: Watch signs, calls, questions, meals, and conversations establish Jesus in public movement.
phases.title: First Signs and Encounters

phases.orientation: Attend to blessings, commands, prayer, possessions, judgment, mission, and authority across complete teaching units.
phases.title: Kingdom Teaching

phases.title: Healing, Authority, and Mercy

phases.orientation: Follow disputes about Sabbath, signs, authority, witnesses, identity, and the words that intensify opposition.

phases.orientation: Hold each parable and prayer instruction within its hearers, setting, sequence, and stated question.

phases.orientation: Trace the long approach through mission, meals, reversals, teaching, healing, wealth, and repeated passion disclosure.
phases.title: The Journey to Jerusalem

phases.orientation: Read judgment speech, future discourse, servant action, farewell teaching, and prayer without collapsing their audiences.

phases.title: Supper, Gethsemane, and Arrest

phases.orientation: Keep the hearings, mockery, crucifixion, sayings, death, witnesses, and burial sequences source-specific.

phases.orientation: Inspect tomb witnesses, appearances, recognition, commissioning, restoration, and departure in their distinct order.

phases.orientation: Attend to witness, Lamb imagery, conflict, reign, city, testimony, and the closing promise of coming.

character.throughline: Earlier sources are explicitly applied to Jesus; the personal name Jesus is commanded before birth; Christ appears as translated Messiah, title, confession, proclamation, and stable combined identifier; the Gospel witnesses preserve his ministry, relationships, death, and resurrection; Acts and the letters proclaim and remember him; Revelation closes with his promised coming.
